Euclid I43Extended

AreaGeometryConstructions
Game: This is a picture, not a game: move the point inside the slanted box and watch three coloured pieces keep their sizes matched.
How to play: Drag a corner or the point X, or focus one and use the arrow keys. Tick “areas on the same side of BD” to see the orange pair, and use the two buttons to put X on either side of the diagonal.
Look for the math

Plain Euclid I.43 only talks about a point on the diagonal. This applet, following a construction of Quang Tuan Bui, keeps a matching piece when X moves off that line — and the same matching works on either side.

What Euclid I.43 says

Through X draw MP parallel to BC (M on AB, P on CD) and NQ parallel to AB (N on BC, Q on AD). Write X = A + t(B − A) + u(D − A) and call the parallelogram's area S. Then AMXQ has area t×u×S and XNCP has area (1−t)×(1−u)×S. The diagonal BD is exactly t + u = 1, which makes those two areas equal: the Elements I.43.

Off the diagonal

Inside triangle ABD we have t + u < 1, so the blue piece XNCP is larger than the red one AMXQ. Now make Y = B + D − X, so XBYD is a parallelogram; let R be where DY meets NQ, and draw RS parallel to BC with S on AB. A short calculation gives ASRQ = (1−t)(1−u)S = XNCP. That is the page's central claim, and the logic test confirms it for 1,932 placements of X — both below and above BD. The leftover strip MSRX has area (1−t−u)S below BD (and (t+u−1)S above it), exactly the difference between the blue and red pieces.

The same-side pair

Tick the box and the applet draws a second pair of congruent-looking orange pieces QXUV and XMSR. Their areas are both (1−t)(1−u)S − t×u×S = |1−t−u|S, so they match each other and measure the gap. The page also says the intersection T of RS and UV lies on AX; in these coordinates T = ((1−t)(1−u)/u, (1−t)(1−u)/t), whose two coordinates have the same ratio as X, so T is on that line. The test checks all of this in every placement, including points on BD where the gap is zero.

Why the article's proof works

Let W be where DR meets AB, K where RS meets CD, and E and F where the line through W parallel to BC meets NQ and CD. Because SWER and BWRX are parallelograms, ER = BW − NR = RX − NR = NX, so REFK and XNCP are congruent. In parallelogram AWFD, R lies on diagonal WD, and Euclid I.43 gives ASRQ = REFK; together, ASRQ = XNCP. Tick “proof lines” to see W, E, F and K. The logic test checks REFK = XNCP for every configuration too.

Try this: put X just below BD, note the gap in the status line, then press “X above BD” and watch the same construction turn the gap into the other side's difference.
